title: The hunter's arrow
hook: a hunter's arrow strikes Krishna, and Krishna sends the hunter to heaven
carry: god's grace reaches even the one who wounded him
tomorrow: one name in Vishnu's line surprises people. whose, and why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Gita's rhythm: whenever dharma slips, god comes again, yuge yuge, age after age. Today, the end of his time on earth, and the hunter who caused it.

A phone knocked into a pool. A borrowed car with a fresh dent. A friend who did real damage without meaning to and now can't stop saying sorry. The Bhagavata Purana tells one of these at the very end of Krishna's life. A hunter named Jara sees something move among the leaves near the sea, takes it for a deer, and lets an arrow fly. It isn't a deer. It's Krishna's foot. Jara runs up, sees whom he has hit, and falls at his feet, shaking. And the first thing Krishna says to him is: don't be afraid. Get up.
screen: `DAMAGE NOBODY MEANT.` → `AN ARROW FOR A DEER.` → `DON'T BE AFRAID. GET UP.`

segments.voice: The scene is already sorrowful before the arrow flies. Krishna's own clan, the Yadus, has torn itself apart in a drunken quarrel by the sea, and his brother Balarama has already left the world. Krishna sits quietly under a tree, one foot resting across his thigh. Then the arrow. Jara begs him: I did this without knowing. Punish me. Krishna's answer turns the whole scene. Don't be afraid, Jara. Get up. This happened by my own wish. And then the part that stuns people: Krishna sends the hunter to heaven. Jara circles him, bows, and is carried up. Look at what Krishna doesn't do. He doesn't make Jara earn it, or wait for a better apology. The wounded one is the one who gives. Many teachers read this as grace, kripa in Sanskrit: the Lord's gift, given freely, reaching even the hand that hurt him. And by my own wish says one more thing Hindus hold about Krishna: his coming and going are his lila, his play, not something done to him. Then he leaves the world, and the Bhagavata adds a line that matters for these weeks: on the day he went, the age of Kali came in.
screen: `A CLAN FALLS APART BY THE SEA.` · `AN ARROW, MEANT FOR A DEER.` · `DON'T BE AFRAID. THIS WAS MY WISH.` · `THE HUNTER, SENT TO HEAVEN.` · then, large: `GRACE REACHES THE ONE WHO WOUNDED HIM.`

segments.voice: Fold your hands. Many Hindus close their worship with a short prayer asking forgiveness for anything done wrong, knowingly or not. Say it once in your own words: for whatever I did without knowing, forgive me. Then, on each breath out, let someone who hurt you without meaning to come to mind, and hold them in that same light. If you don't pray, simply sit with both.
Krishna: struck by a hunter's stray arrow at the end of his life, he told the hunter don't be afraid, and sent him to heaven.
Your line: God's grace reaches even the one who wounded him. Jara went up, not down. Day fifteen fifty-nine, done.

screen: `DAY 1559 COUNTS.` → `GOD'S GRACE REACHES EVEN THE ONE WHO WOUNDED HIM.` → `TOMORROW: ONE NAME SURPRISES PEOPLE. WHOSE?`

fork.setup: your little cousin hears the ending and says: the hunter should've been punished! what does Krishna do in the Bhagavata?

fork.reveal: Jara begged to be punished. Krishna said don't be afraid, this was my wish, and sent him to heaven. many teachers call it kripa, grace.

original.note: Sanskrit: don't be afraid, Krishna's first words to the hunter Jara.

Jara.meaning: the hunter whose arrow struck Krishna's foot

Kali.meaning: the dark age, last of the four ages (yugas)

lila.meaning: play: God's free coming and going in the world

notes: Krishna run, day 4 of 4 (1556–1559). Angle: his departure, read as forgiveness that starts with the frightened person. For parents: this is a death scene, told gently, with no crisis content; it is fine to pause on it with a child.

Details from Bhagavata 11.30: the Yadus' drunken quarrel at Prabhasa; Balarama leaving first; Krishna seated under a tree with his foot on his thigh; Jara mistakes the foot for a deer; Krishna says 'ma bhair jare, uttishtha', it was his own wish, and sends Jara to heaven. Krishna then speaks to his charioteer Daruka, so the script avoids calling Jara the last person he speaks to. Confirm each.
Original 'मा भैः' (ma bhaih) is the form behind 'ma bhair' in the verse; confirm spelling.
'On the day Krishna went back, the age of Kali came in' paraphrases Bhagavata 12.2 (around verses 29–33). Confirm the verse.
